title: Credibility and the Pressure to Publish
text:
Academic research depends on its credibility, which in turn rests on transparency in methodology. A consensus among researchers rarely emerges from a single study, but from the gradual accumulation of evidence over time.

Critics argue that the pressure to publish has eroded this rigour, encouraging authors to emphasise novelty over reproducibility. Such a tendency, they contend, undermines public trust in science, since findings that cannot be replicated carry little authority.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does the credibility of research depend on?
options: The size of the research budget
The number of pages in a journal

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do critics say the pressure to publish encourages?
options: Authors to emphasise novelty over reproducibility

questions.text: What does the author imply about a single study?
options: It can establish a firm consensus on its own
It rarely settles a question on its own
It is always more reliable than many smaller studies
It should be ignored by researchers

questions.text: What can be inferred about findings that cannot be replicated?
options: They are the most valuable contribution to science
They are likely to weaken public trust in research
They are usually confirmed by later studies
They are unrelated to research methodology

vocabulary.definition: the quality of being trusted and believed
general agreement among a group of people
careful and thorough attention to accuracy and detail
the ability of results to be obtained again by others

paragraph_translations: Wiarygodność wyników badań naukowych zależy od przejrzystości zastosowanej metodologii. Konsensus wśród badaczy rzadko powstaje na podstawie jednego badania, lecz wyłania się stopniowo, wraz z gromadzeniem dowodów w czasie.

Krytycy twierdzą, że presja na publikowanie osłabiła tę rzetelność, zachęcając autorów do kładzenia nacisku na nowatorstwo zamiast na powtarzalność wyników. Ich zdaniem taka tendencja podważa zaufanie społeczne do nauki, ponieważ wyniki, których nie da się powtórzyć, mają niewielki autorytet.
